Source-specific feature priority: Retain the actual visible source facial hair with its correct extent and color; eyes, upper-lip moustache, source-shaped open or closed creature mouth, chin beard in that top-to-bottom order. No invented hair from shadows.

Use case: compositing.
Asset type: one full-resolution Hearts of Iron IV character portrait replacement with the original source composition and aspect ratio. Keep the tool's full image detail and output resolution; game display sizing is handled separately.
Proportion priority: start from the reference mascot's nearly round head and curved chin, seated directly into a broadened EXISTING collar with no exposed vertical neck column. Preserve source pose and head angle without copying the human head/neck length; adapt the existing shoulders and collar to meet that compact anatomy. This does not add a collar to a bare or wrap-only source.
Image 1 is the original HOI4 portrait and composition target. Image 2 is the user's exact 奶龙 identity reference: a smooth golden-yellow round creature with green rings around black eyes, a small horizontal mouth and creamy belly.
Replace the human head, body and exposed human skin with this recognizable yellow mascot. RETAIN the original person's visible hairstyle, hairline, hair color and eyebrows as distinguishing features attached to the mascot, adapting them to its round head. Match the original's parting, thickness and curls. Facial hair is conditional, never a default: copy moustache, beard or sideburns only when actually visible in this source, with its exact extent and color. Otherwise keep the upper lip and chin smooth yellow. Dark skin shading, nose shadows and lip creases are not facial hair. Preserve a bald scalp where the source has one and do not invent hair hidden under a hat.
Preserve the original garment design, uniform type, fabric, colors, headgear, glasses, decorations, accessories, expression, gaze, pose, action, framing, lighting, background and painterly color treatment. WHERE THE SOURCE HAS A GARMENT COLLAR, retailor its neck opening and shoulder fit to the mascot rather than copying a narrow human neck opening. If the source is unclothed or has only a scarf/wrap, preserve that state without inventing a shirt, uniform or tailored collar. Keep all existing garment design details and insignia; do not invent new hats, uniforms, medals or symbols. Use only visually present features; do not infer appearance from filenames or historical biographies.
Keep the yellow creature's anatomy and large green-ringed black eyes; do not restore human skin, human nose or human ears. Adapt its small reference mouth to the exact source expression: an open toothy smile stays open and toothy, a parted mouth stays parted, and a closed serious mouth stays closed. Express the original mood through its creature eyes and mouth plus retained eyebrows; do not flatten all expressions into a neutral horizontal line.
Facial-hair placement: wherever the original has a moustache and chin beard, their top-to-bottom order is eyes, UPPER-LIP moustache, source-shaped open or closed creature mouth, chin beard. Never place the visible mouth above the moustache or turn the moustache into a second beard. Clean-shaven originals stay clean-shaven.
When the source actually has a moustache, show it as a distinct visible band of hair with fine painted hair texture ABOVE the mascot's existing grey lip and small mouth. The reference mascot's normal grey lip wedge or its shadow does not count as facial hair; do not merely recolor that lip and omit the moustache. Retain a narrow readable separation between the hair and mouth. Apply this only to genuinely visible source facial hair; clean-shaven sources retain the normal bare mascot mouth.
Retain the visible shape, symbol count and arrangement of source collar patches and existing decorations. Do not invent chest medallions. Any source note markings that are illegible remain indistinct texture; do not invent readable serial numbers, identification codes, words or labels.
Collar and anatomy: use a compact rounded mascot head seated close to broad shoulders, with a very short, wide neck transition. No tall cylindrical/giraffe neck or long tapered yellow stalk. When a garment collar exists in the source, the entire neck base must fit INSIDE its correctly sized opening. Widen and reshape that original opening naturally around the base while keeping its style, tabs, piping and badges. Collar front sits visibly in front of the lower neck; collar back sits behind it, with coherent perspective, contact shadow and fabric tension. No neck clipping through collar, pinched narrow ring, floating collar, broken seam or abrupt geometric junction. The creamy belly stays under opaque clothing wherever clothing is present; never add a cream/white bib on the neck. Respect this fit even for tiny advisor or pilot portraits; it does not authorize inventing clothes on bare figures.
The head silhouette is nearly round or a SHORT egg shape. Its chin rests immediately above the garment collar, without copying the original human neck length. Preserve the shoulder position and crop by broadening the fitted garment; do not fill that space with a tall yellow column.
Where the source has clothing at the neck, that garment meets the underside of a visibly rounded chin. There is no separate exposed vertical neck column between head and collar, including bald and three-quarter-view portraits. Bare or scarf-only sources retain their original clothing state.
The lower head silhouette curves inward toward its base instead of continuing down as parallel straight yellow sides. Raise and broaden an EXISTING collar and shoulders to meet that curved chin; do not insert an extra yellow neck roll underneath it or add a collar where the original has none.
Keep the source's fastening state: a buttoned closed standing collar remains closed and buttoned, with both front ends meeting naturally at the center seam. Do not turn a closed military collar into a deep V-neck or unbuttoned shirt. Preserve open lapels/shirt collars only where the original is actually open.
Preserve the source aspect ratio, crop and number of figures. Preserve real alpha transparency, photographic frames, note cards and existing decorative markings where present. This instruction applies only when the original has a photo frame; never add a frame or note to a standalone portrait. This condition preserves every symbol that is actually clear in the original; it does not remove or replace a visible source emblem.

Man wearing broad white wrapped turban and dark patterned draped robe, dark moustache and compact dark beard, bare visible eyes. Slight leftward head; preserve actual cloth wrapping, beard outline and deep source shadows, no invented spectacles. Retain original clothing style, open/closed layers, actual accessories/fittings, head angle, gaze, expression, lighting and crop. Fit the compact near-round yellow mascot head to a VERY SHORT BROAD neck and broad mascot shoulders at the actual garment. Adapt collar circumference and shoulder position naturally;no long neck stalk, floating collar, cream bib or newly closed open V.
Final source-specific check: Retain the actual visible source facial hair with its correct extent and color; eyes, upper-lip moustache, source-shaped open or closed creature mouth, chin beard in that top-to-bottom order. No invented hair from shadows.

Keep any genuine source outer-edge alpha falloff only at that actual exterior boundary; preserve actual source transparency rather than making the subject itself translucent.
